editorial_contributions.text:
The authors study the integer and rational coefficient cohomology of real partial flag manifolds.

They give an algorithm to compute the integer cohomology groups of any real partial flag manifold, by computing the incidence coefficients of the Schubert cells. Real flag manifolds also have a cell decomposition, however the boundary maps are no longer trivial. For even flag manifolds they determine the integer cohomology groups, by proving that any torsion class has order \(2\). Also they conjecture that this holds for any real flag manifold. They obtain results concerning which Schubert varieties represent integer cohomology classes, their structure constants and how to express them in terms of characteristic classes. For even flag manifolds and Grassmannians they also describe Schubert calculus. The Schubert calculus can be used to obtain lower bounds for certain real enumerative geometry problems.

title.title: On the cohomology rings of real flag manifolds: Schubert cycles

editorial_contributions.text: The authors generalize previous computations of \textit{M. Wendt} [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 24, No. 1, 1--48 (2024; Zbl 1562.14012)]. Precisely they establish formulae describing the Witt-sheaf cohomology rings of partial flag varieties in type A in terms of the Pontryagin classes of the sub-quotient bundles (see Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.2). The methods of establishing the result are very close to the corresponding results for integral cohomology of real flag manifolds [\textit{Á. K. Matszangosz}, Math. Ann. 381, No. 3--4, 1537--1588 (2021; Zbl 1490.14085)]. A motivation for these results is the long-term goal of establishing a version of Schubert calculus in the algebraic setting of Witt-sheaf cohomology.

title.title: Chow-Witt rings and topology of flag varieties

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(\mathrm{Gr}_{k} (n)\) denote the real Grassmannian of \(k\)-planes in \(\mathbb{R}^{n}\). It is classical and well-known that the mod \(2\) cohomology ring \(H^{*}(\mathrm{Gr}_{k}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2})\) has a presentation in terms of the Stiefel-Whitney classes of the tautological \(k\)-plane bundle over \(\mathrm{Gr}_{k}(n)\) (see e.g., [\textit{A. Borel}, Comment. Math. Helv. 27, 165--197 (1953; Zbl 0052.40301)]).
Let \(\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{k} (n)\) be the \textit{oriented} real Grassmannian of \textit{oriented} \(k\)-planes in \(\mathbb{R}^{n}\). Clearly we have a double covering \(\pi: \widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{k}(n) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}_{k} (n)\).
It might be surprising that the mod \(2\) cohomology structure of \(\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{k}(n)\) is still unclear except for \(k = 1, 2\). Even the mod \(2\) Betti numbers for \(\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{k}(n)\) have been unknown until recently (see [\textit{T. Ozawa}, Osaka J. Math. 59, No. 4, 843--851 (2022; Zbl 1540.57051)]).
The ``standard'' approach to investigate the mod \(2\) cohomology ring \(H^{*}(\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{k}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2})\) is perhaps to make use of the Gysin exact sequence associated to the above double covering.
Then we know that \(H^{*}(\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{k}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2})\) sits in the following short exact sequence
\[
0 \longrightarrow C
\overset{\pi^{*}}{\longrightarrow}
H^{*}(\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{k}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2})
\overset{\delta}{\longrightarrow}
K 
\longrightarrow 0,
\]
where \(C\) and \(K\) are respectively the cokernel and the kernel of the map \(w_{1}: H^{*}(\mathrm{Gr}_{k}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2}) \longrightarrow H^{* + 1}(\mathrm{Gr}_{k}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2})\) given by the multiplication of the first Stiefel-Whitney class \(w_{1}\) of the tautological \(k\)-plane bundle over \(\mathrm{Gr}_{k}(n)\).
The ring \(C\) is fairly easy to describe. It is just the quotient ring of \(H^{*}(\mathrm{Gr}_{k}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2})\) by the ideal generated by \(w_{1}\).
The real difficulty is that one does not know how to find cohomology classes that generate the \(C\)-module \(K\).

In the paper under review, the authors identify this module using certain Koszul complexes, which involves the syzygies between the relations defining \(C\). Using this new technique, the authors obtain the presentation of \(H^{*}(\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_{3}(n); \mathbb{F}_{2})\) for \(2^{t-1} < n \leq 2^{t} - 4\) with \(t \geq 4\), which complements known descriptions in the cases \(n = 2^{t} - i\), \(i = 0, 1, 2, 3\) with \(t \geq 3\).
The authors also discuss various issues that arise for the cases \(k > 3\), supported by computer calculation.
